Hi Priya / Kunal —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size pricing properly: 

Recap from our demo
- Use case: customer support summarization + routing for premium accounts; ingest recent 12 mos of context to improve agent handoffs.
- Preferred UX: short prompt (~200 tokens) + concise completion (~120–180 tokens) for summaries; longer completions (~600–800 tokens) for case writeups in escalations.
- Expected peak concurrency: ~45 rps for summaries during business hours, baseline 8 rps off-hours.

Open items we need from you to firm up a ballpark $/1M tokens target and whether 8k vs 32k context is necessary:
1) Average prompt tokens: can you confirm typical prompt length in production (examples: full email thread included, or just the last 2 messages)?
2) Completion target mix: what percentage of requests are short summaries (<=200 tokens) vs long writeups (>=600 tokens)?
3) Percent of requests requiring >8k context (e.g., include full customer history) vs those fitting comfortably in 8k.
4) Monthly token budget target or top-of-funnel $/1M tokens target (helps us recommend quant/pipeline).

I've attached a quick worksheet (RDW-token-estimates.xlsx) that shows a few pricing scenarios (8k/32k/128k) and per-request examples — fill the yellow cells and we can produce a tailored estimate.

Next steps we'd propose:
- You fill the worksheet with sample prompt/completion counts and monthly expected volumes (by Tue).
- Aditya will run a short profile based on your inputs and recommend batching/quantization to hit target $/1M tokens.
- We produce an initial SOW + recommended config for Dedicated capacity if volumes justify it.

If easier, we can do a 20-min follow-up tomorrow to walk through the worksheet. Which time works?

Best,

Thanks Jasmine — great session. Quick answers so you can start modeling: 

1) Average prompt tokens: ~220 tokens when we include the last two messages + metadata. For escalation cases where we include three recent exchanges + ticket notes, closer to ~850 tokens.
2) Completion mix: ~78% short summaries (120–180 tokens), ~18% medium responses (300–500 tokens), ~4% long writeups (~600–900 tokens).
3) Context needs: ~12% of requests need >8k because they pull the full ticket thread + KB snippets. About 2% will likely need 32k for rare enterprise escalations where we attach long logs.
4) Budget: initial target is a unit economics ceiling of $750 per 1M tokens — we know that's conservative, but we need to see if Redwood can meet that with caching/batching.

We'll try to populate your spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow. If you can, please also include an estimate assuming we enable prefix (conversation) caching; I think that will materially lower cost on summaries.

—Priya

Priya / Kunal —

Thanks for the fast turnaround on numbers, that's very helpful. A couple notes from an engineering/ops perspective as we model costs: 

- Profiling assumptions: I'll model three canonical request types: summary_short (prompt 220 / completion 150), escalation_medium (prompt 850 / completion 400), escalation_long (prompt 2,800 / completion 700) — the last is for cases where you pull a lot of ticket history into the prompt.
- Context strategy: For the 12% that need >8k we should split them: ~10% use 16–32k context with KV cache disabled for long histories; ~2% we should provision 32k/128k fallback for log-heavy escalations.
- Cost levers: batching, prefix caching, and a mixed-quant model (float16 for long-context workers, int8/4-bit for short summaries) will almost always be necessary to hit $750/1M tokens at scale. I'll run both hosted and Dedicated (reserved GPU) scenarios.

I attached an engineer's note (inline below) and will drop a populated worksheet by 9:30am PT with per-request cost, tokens/month, and expected $/1M for 8k vs 32k vs 128k.

Inline engineer note:
- Short summaries: optimize for latency (lower seq len, batched inference, cached KV). Expect unit cost to be 35–55% of long-context requests after caching.
- Medium/long: higher memory footprint; use quantization and model routing to cheaper variants for mostly generation-heavy workloads.
- Fallbacks: route to lower-throughput but cheaper instances when Dedicated capacity is saturated — reduces 95% p99 tail risk.

Will follow up with the worksheet and a short table.

-Aditya
